nor the food of an apostate ascetic, nor likewise of an oil-presser, / nor likewise the food of an outcaste uninvited by a brahmin.
Having unintentionally eaten the food of any one of these, one should fast for three days; / having eaten it intentionally, or semen, feces, and urine, one should perform a kṛcchra penance.
Having intentionally eaten the food of one who has committed a major sin, / of an impure father after childbirth, or of a leather-worker, a twice-born must perform a kṛcchra penance.
Having eaten the food of a caṇḍāla or a dog-cooker, one should perform a cāndrāyaṇa penance; / likewise [for eating] the food of a deceased person within four days, or food smelled by a cow,
or the leftovers of a śūdra, light leftovers, or the food of a woman in childbed; / one should perform a taptakṛcchra penance for the pacification of that sin.
Having eaten during the ritual impurity of a brahmin, a twice-born should perform a sāntapana penance; / but having eaten during the ritual impurity of a kṣatriya, a kṛcchra penance is prescribed.
Having eaten during the ritual impurity of a vaiśya, one should perform a taptakṛcchra penance; / having eaten during the ritual impurity of a śūdra, a twice-born should perform a cāndrāyaṇa penance.

2.15.m:
Whoever eats during someone's ritual impurity also becomes impure in that manner, / for as long as that person's ritual impurity is proclaimed to last, O Rāma.
When that ritual impurity has passed, he should perform expiation; / and having eaten during the ritual impurity of a superior, he should fast for a day.
Having drunk water from a well containing a dead five-clawed animal / or once combined with impure matter, a foremost twice-born should remain fasting for three days;
a kṣatriya should remain so for two days, and a vaiśya for one day; / and a śūdra, eating only at night, is purified by the five products of the cow.
Having eaten astringent substances and drunk impure fluids, a twice-born / remains impure for as long as the food passes downward.
Having consumed the urine or feces of a domestic pig, a donkey, a camel, / a jackal, or of an animal called a monkey, a twice-born should perform a cāndrāyaṇa penance.
Having eaten dried meats, mushrooms grown on the ground, / and unknown meat kept at a slaughterhouse, one should perform this very vow.

2.15.m:
One who eats [the flesh of] carnivorous animals, pigs, camels, jackals, monkeys, or crows, / [or of] oxen, men, horses, donkeys, or camels, and those that have five nails,
and having eaten elephant meat, becomes purified by the taptakṛcchra penance. / Having eaten village fowl or mushrooms, one must perform the cāndrāyaṇa penance.
Even when [food] is contaminated with hair or insects, one should drink [the decoction of] brahmasuvarcalā. / Having eaten likewise at an āmaśrāddha, one becomes purified by the taptakṛcchra penance.
Having eaten likewise [food] intended [for the gods or ancestors before it is offered], there should be a fast of three nights. / Having eaten likewise honey and meat, O Bhārgava, one observing a vow,
as well as garlic, carrots, onions, and liquor, / and whatever is similar to garlic and the like in smell, O best of men,
or having eaten [the flesh] of a carnivorous bird, one must perform the cāndrāyaṇa penance for a month; / likewise [avoid] red tree-resins and exudations from diseased places,
śelu fruit, bovine colostrum, poison, śleṣmātaka fruit, earth, / [and] vainly prepared kṛsara, saṃyāva, milk-rice, cakes, and fried pastries.

शुभैः पुष्पफलैर्यानि भक्तैरभियुतानि च ॥
विष्किराञ्जालपादांश्च रक्तपादांस्तथैव च॥38॥
सर्वशुष्कांश्च चूडालान्प्रतोदांश्च विवर्जयेत् ॥
वर्तिको वर्तिका चेति तित्तिरश्च कपिञ्जलः ॥ 39 ॥
भक्ष्यो मयूरश्च तथा पक्षिणां ये विवर्जिताः ॥
शशकः शल्लको गोधा खड्गः कूर्मस्तथैव च॥2.73.40॥
भक्ष्याः पञ्चनखाः प्रोक्ताः परिवेषाश्च वर्जिताः ॥
पाठीनान्रोहितान्मत्स्याम्̐ल्लोहतुण्डांश्च भक्षयेत् ॥ 41॥
राजीवांश्च सशल्कांश्च भक्ष्यानाहुर्मनीषिणः ॥
अतोऽन्यान्वर्जयेत्सर्वांस्तथा वै जलचारिणः ॥ 42॥
2.15.m:
Excepting [the milk] of cows, buffaloes, and goats, / all milks are to be avoided, as well as theirs within ten days of calving.
One should avoid [the milk] of a cow in heat, of one eating impure things, or of one whose calf has died; / and all sour substances are to be avoided, with the exception of curds,
and those combined with auspicious flowers, fruits, and grains. / [Avoid] scratchers, web-footed birds, and red-footed ones,
all dried [meats], crested birds, and those that strike with their beaks. / The vartika and the vartikā, the partridge and the kapiñjala,
and the peacock may be eaten, among birds that are [otherwise] excluded. / The hare, the porcupine, the monitor lizard, the rhinoceros, and the turtle:
these five-nailed animals are declared fit to eat, and the rest are forbidden. / One may eat pāṭhīna, rohita, and iron-beaked fish,
and the wise declare rājīva fish and scaly fish to be fit to eat. / Apart from these, one should avoid all others, especially aquatic creatures.

2.15.m:
From eating these [forbidden ones], O Rāma, there should be a fast of three nights. / [Having eaten] a ruddy goose, an aquatic fowl, a swan, a lapwing, or a cormorant,
a raven, a parrot, a vulture, a dātyūha bird, or a myna, / or a crane, a hawk, or an egret, one must observe [a fast of] six nights.
A fast is likewise to be observed upon eating meat from a slaughterhouse. / Goats, sheep, anuroha deer, spotted deer, buffaloes,
raṅku deer, nyaṅku deer, blackbucks, and wild oxen one may eat. / Having eaten the meat of any other than these, one should remain hungry for three days.
All products made of barley and wheat, modifications of milk, / rāga, ṣāḍava, cukra, and whatever contains oil or ghee:
excepting these, having eaten stale food, one should fast for a day. / If a foremost twice-born drinks water contained in a liquor vessel out of delusion,
he should drink milk boiled with śaṅkhapuṣpī for three days. / Having drunk [water] contained in an intoxicating liquor vessel, he should drink [it] likewise for seven nights.

2.15.m:
Having drunk from the leftover of a śūdra, he should drink [it] likewise for five nights. / If a celibate student of the twice-born involuntarily discharges semen in a dream,
having bathed and worshipped the sun, he should recite the verse 'punarmām' three times. / A brahmin who wilfully neglects the fire of his Agnihotra
should observe the cāndrāyaṇa penance for a month; the 'heroic seat' is also beneficial. / Killing a brahmin, drinking liquor, stealing, and violating the teacher's bed,
they declare to be great sins, as well as association with those [who commit them]. / Falsehood in asserting excellence, calumny that reaches the king,
and false obstinacy toward a teacher are equal to killing a brahmin. / Forgetting the Veda, reviling the Vedas, giving false testimony, slaying a friend,
and eating forbidden food or drinks are the six sins equal to drinking liquor. / Stealing a deposit, or a man, a horse, or silver,
or land, diamonds, and gems is remembered as equal to the theft of gold. / Sowing seed in women of one's own kin, in maidens, and in outcast women,
or in the wives of a friend or a son, they know to be equal to violating the teacher's bed. / Killing a cow, sacrificing for those unfit to sacrifice, adultery, selling oneself,

2.15.m:
eating moderately and keeping his senses restrained, to remove the sin of killing a brahmin; / or he should bestow all his property upon a brahmin who knows the Veda.
Or wealth sufficient for life, or a house together with its furnishings.
Through these observances, O twice-born one, one should dispel the condition of a perpetrator of major sins.
One tainted by a minor sin who has killed a cow should eat barley for a month,
or having committed the sin, he should dwell covered with its hide.
He should eat at the fourth mealtime a measured amount of food free from alkali and salt;
with senses restrained, he should bathe with cow's urine for two months.
By day he should follow those cows, and standing upright he should drink water;
having attended to them and paid homage, he should sit in the hero's posture at night.
When they stand he should stand, and when they walk he should follow;
when they are seated he should likewise sit, restrained and free from envy.
A cow that is afflicted, sprinkled [by danger], threatened by perils such as thieves or tigers,
or fallen into mud, he should rescue with all his vital strength.
In heat, heavy rain, or extreme cold, or when the wind blows violently,
he must not protect himself without first protecting the cow to the best of his ability.

Whether in his own or others' house, field, or threshing floor,
he should not announce a cow that is eating, nor a calf that is suckling.
Having completed the observance, he should indeed give [ten] cows with a bull as the eleventh;
if he possesses none, he should present all his property to those learned in the Veda.
In tying, penning, or harnessing, when injury
or death of cattle occurs, he is tainted by the cause there.
He should perform one quarter [penance] in the cowpen, two quarters in tying;
in harnessing it should be one quarter less [i.e. three quarters], and he should perform the whole in striking down.
In wildernesses, impassable places, rough terrain, or caves,
if an accident occurs there, one quarter [penance] is prescribed.
In the faults of injury and death, one should likewise assign half
in taming, riding, penning, and yoking a cart.
If it dies in a river or in traps of splinters, he should perform two quarters.
When many [cattle] perish in tying or penning,
or if a physician acts improperly here, he should perform double the cow-observance.

he should drink barley gruel until the cow becomes healthy.
If, by fate, a single cow should be killed by many,
they should perform one quarter of [the penance for] cow-killing, each individually.
In [restraining with] an instrument for the medical treatment of a cow, or in delivering a dead fetus,
if an accident occurs there, no guilt is found there.
And when one gives medicine, oil, or food to brahmins and others,
if an accident occurs while it is being given, no guilt attaches to the giver.
Those guilty of minor sins should likewise perform this very observance.
One who has broken his vow of celibacy [should perform] this or the cāndrāyaṇa for purification.
At the seventh period, the vow-breaker at a crossroads,
sacrifices silently at night according to the rule for simple domestic sacrifices;
having offered oblations into the fire according to rule, then with the verse "samiddho 'ñjan..."
he should offer oblations with clarified butter to Vāta, Indra, Guru, and Vahni.

2.15.m:
therefore a brahmin, a kṣatriya, and a vaiśya should not drink liquor.
Liquor is to be known as threefold: made from molasses, made from flour, and made from honey.
Just as one, so all should not be drunk by the best of the twice-born.
Liquor, meat, and the drinking of intoxicants belong to yakṣas, rākṣasas, and piśācas;
that must not be eaten by a brahmin who eats the oblation of the gods.
[Intoxicant] made from madhūka, from sugarcane, from wood-apple, from jujube, from date, from jackfruit,
from grape-juice, from wild grapes, mereya, and that produced from coconut—
these ten intoxicating liquors are not to be consumed by a brahmin.
He whose knowledge of the Veda, reached at will, is once flooded by liquor,
his brahminhood departs and he becomes a śūdra.
Hereafter I shall declare the decision regarding the theft of gold.
A brahmin who has committed theft of gold, having approached the king,
and confessing his deed, should say: "May your majesty punish me."
Taking up a club, the king himself should strike him once.

One-fourth of [the penance for] killing a brahmin is prescribed for the slaying of a kṣatriya.
In the case of a vaiśya, [the penalty is] an eighth part, but in the case of a śūdra it is known as a sixteenth. / However, having unintentionally killed a kṣatriya, the best of the twice-born
should give one thousand cows along with a bull for his own purification; / or, restrained, with matted hair, he should observe for three years the penance of a killer of a brahmin.
He should dwell far from the village, having his abode at the foot of a tree. / The best of the twice-born should observe this very penance for a year
after killing a vaiśya who follows proper conduct, and should give one hundred cows. / The killer of a śūdra should observe this entire penance for six months,
or he may give to a brahmin eleven white cows along with a bull. / Having killed a cat or a mongoose, a blue jay or a frog,
or a dog, an iguana, an owl, or a crow, he should observe the penance for killing a śūdra; / or he should drink milk for three nights, or walk the distance of a yojana,

and for shrubs, creeping vines, climbers, and flowering plants. / Upon the slaughter of a thousand boneless creatures,

and for those originating from fruits and flowers, sipping ghee is the purification. / For cultivated medicinal plants and for those that have grown by themselves in the forest,
if destroyed in vain, he should follow a cow for one day, taking only milk. / By these penances, the sin arising from injury is to be removed.

Hear the rule of the penances that remove the fault of theft. / Having stolen grain or wealth intentionally, the best of the twice-born,
if from the house of a member of his own varna, is purified by a year-long kṛcchra penance. / But for the abduction of men, of women, and [the theft] of a field or a house,
and of the water of wells and tanks, the purification is traditionally said to be a cāndrāyaṇa penance. / Having committed the theft of articles of small value from another's house,
he should observe the sāntapana kṛcchra penance after returning it, for his own purification. / For stealing food to be chewed or swallowed, a vehicle, a bed, or a seat,
and flowers, roots, or fruits, the five products of the cow are the purifier. / For [stealing] grass, wood, trees, dry food, and raw sugar,
and cloth, leather, or meat, there should be fasting for three nights. / For [stealing] gems, pearls, corals, copper, or silver,
and iron, bronze, or stones, he should eat broken grains of rice for twelve days. / For [stealing] cotton, silk, or wool, and cloven-hoofed or single-hoofed animals,

One should dispel [the sin] incurred with a forbidden woman by these penances: / one should perform the penance for violating the Guru's bed after emitting semen into unnatural wombs,
and with the wives of a friend or a son, with maidens, and with outcaste women, / with a paternal aunt, a sister, or a sister's daughter, or a maternal aunt,
and having approached a daughter of a maternal uncle, one should observe a cāndrāyaṇa penance. / A wise man should not take these three as wives;
kinswomen are not to be married, and marrying [the kinswoman] of one's father, one falls low. / A man who emits semen into non-human females, or into a menstruating woman, or into unnatural orifices,
or into water, should observe the sāntapana kṛcchra penance. / But having engaged in sexual intercourse with a man or with a woman,
or in a cow-drawn cart, or by day, a twice-born should bathe with his clothes on. / Through sexual union with a Caṇḍāla or an outcaste woman, through eating [her food], or through accepting gifts [from her],

then a kṛcchra and a cāndrāyaṇa penance are traditionally held to be her purification. / The sin that a twice-born incurs in a single night by serving a low-caste woman,
he dispels in three years, living on alms and chanting [sacred texts] daily. / This expiation has been declared for the evildoers among all four [varnas];
hear these expiations for those who associate with fallen persons. / One who associates with a fallen person for a year becomes fallen
by officiating at sacrifices for him, teaching him, giving to him, speaking with him, drinking with him, eating with him, or sitting with him. / Whichever fallen person among these a man associates with,
he should perform that very [fallen person's] penance for the purification of that association. / Water-libations for a fallen person should be performed together with his sapiṇḍas and kinsmen

एनस्विभिरनिर्णिक्तैर्नार्थं किञ्चित्समाचरेत्॥ 166 ॥
2.15.m:
on an inauspicious day, in the evening, in the presence of kinsmen, priests, and elders. / A maidservant should overturn a jar filled with water, as if for a deceased person, at all times.
They should observe day and night with their kinsmen without ritual impurity; / but from then on, they should cease conversation and sitting together with him.
And the distribution of the inheritance and customary worldly intercourse [cease]; / the eldest's share should be withheld, as well as whatever wealth was obtained by the eldest.
And a younger brother superior in virtue may obtain the eldest's share. / But when the penance has been performed, a new pot full of water
they should bring along with him, having bathed in a sacred body of water. / Having fetched that pot with good water, and entering his own home,
he should perform all rites of kinsmen just as before. / One should perform this very rite also for fallen women.
Clothing, food, and drink should be given [to them], and they should dwell near the house. / One should not engage in any dealings with sinners who have not purified themselves.

2.15.m:
And one should never shun these [sinners] once their purification is performed. / But those who have slain a child, those who are ungrateful, even if purified according to dharma,
and those who slay seekers of refuge, and those who slay women, one should not live with. / Those twice-born for whom the Sāvitrī has not been recited according to rule,
having caused them to perform three kṛcchra penances, one should initiate according to rule. / But as for those twice-born engaged in forbidden acts who desire to perform penance,
and those brahmins who are abandoned, among them one should instruct that [penance]. / Wealth which brahmins acquire by blameworthy action,
they are purified by relinquishing it, and by recitation and ascetic practice alone. / Having recited three thousand [repetitions] of the Sāvitrī with concentrated mind,
drinking milk for a month in a cow-pen, he is released from an unlawful acceptance of gifts. / But him, emaciated by fasting, returned again from the cow-pen,
bowing down, they should ask: 'Gentle one, do you desire to be gentle?' / Having spoken the truth to the brahmins, he should distribute fodder to the cows.

गोभिः प्रवर्तिते तीर्थे कुर्युस्तस्य परिग्रहम ॥
व्रात्यानां याजनं कृत्वा परेषामंत्यकर्म च ॥1 74 ॥
अभिचारमहीनं च त्रिभिः कृच्छ्रैर्विशुध्यति ॥
शरणागतं परित्यज्य वेदं विप्लाव्य च द्विजः॥175॥

होमश्च शाकलो नित्यमपङ्क्त्यानां विशोधनम्॥
उष्ट्रयानं समारुह्य खरयानं च कामतः॥178॥
स्नात्वा तु विप्रो दिग्वासाः प्राणायामेन शुध्यति॥

स्नातकव्रतलोपे च प्रायश्चित्तमभोजनम्॥

2.15.m:
In the sacred place established by the cows, they should receive him. / Having performed sacrifice for outcastes and the funeral rites for others,
and black magic, and an Ahīna sacrifice, one is purified by three kṛcchra penances. / A twice-born who abandons one seeking refuge, and who distorts the Veda,
restraining his food for a year, rids himself of that sin. / Bitten by dogs, jackals, or snakes, or by domestic carnivorous animals,
and by cattle, horses, camels, or boars, one is purified by breath control. / Eating at the sixth mealtime and recitation of the Saṃhitā,
and daily Śākala oblation, is the purification of those unfit to sit in a line. / Having mounted a carriage drawn by camels or a carriage drawn by donkeys intentionally,
a brahmin, having bathed sky-clad, is purified by breath control. / Without [clothes], one should place one's body inside separated waters;
bathing outside with clothes on and touching a cow, he is purified. / Upon the transgression of regular rites enjoined by the Veda,
and on the breach of the vow of a snātaka, the penance is fasting. / Having said 'hum' to a brahmin, or 'thou' to an elder,

for the remaining articles, cleansing of the article is prescribed. / Whoever eats his cooked food, he should be made to perform half a kṛcchra;

2.15.m: a wrongdoer is freed from sin, and others likewise through charity. / In proportion as a man does not speak of his own virtue,

2.15.s:
tathā tathā ca yenaiva tasmātpāpātpramucyate..
kṛtvā pāpaṃ hi smartavyaṃ tasmātpāptpramucyate..233..
2.15.d:
तथा तथा च येनैव तस्मात्पापात्प्रमुच्यते॥
कृत्वा पापं हि स्मर्तव्यं तस्मात्पाप्त्प्रमुच्यते॥233॥
2.15.m: just so is he released from that sin by that very deed; / for having committed a sin, it must be remembered: thereby he is released from the sin.

2.15.s:
yathāyathā manastasya duṣkṛtaṃ karma garhati..
tathātathā śarīraṃ tattenādharmeṇa mucyate..234..
2.15.d:
यथायथा मनस्तस्य दुष्कृतं कर्म गर्हति॥
तथातथा शरीरं तत्तेनाधर्मेण मुच्यते॥234॥
2.15.m: In proportion as his mind censures the evil deed, / so is that body released from that unrighteousness.

2.15.s:
naitatkuryāṃ punariti nivṛtyāṃ prayatennaraḥ..
evaṃ saṃcintya manasā pretyakarmaphalodayam..235..
2.15.d:
नैतत्कुर्यां पुनरिति निवृत्यां प्रयतेन्नरः॥
एवं संचिन्त्य मनसा प्रेत्यकर्मफलोदयम्॥235॥
2.15.m: A man should resolve upon cessation, thinking: 'I will not do this again.' / Reflecting in mind in this manner upon the arising of the fruit of deeds in the hereafter,

2.15.s:
manovākkarmabhirnnityaṃ śubhaṃ karma samācaret..
ajñānādyadi vā jñānātkṛtvā karma vigarhitam..236..
2.15.d:
मनोवाक्कर्मभिर्न्नित्यं शुभं कर्म समाचरेत्॥
अज्ञानाद्यदि वा ज्ञानात्कृत्वा कर्म विगर्हितम्॥236॥
2.15.m: one should constantly perform good action through mind, speech, and deeds. / If, either through ignorance or knowledge, he has committed a censurable deed,

2.15.s:
tasmāddhi mucyate nityaṃ dvitīyaṃ na samācaret..
yasminkarmaṇyasya kṛte manasaḥ syādalāghavam..
tasmiṃstāvattapaḥ kuryādyāvattuṣṭikaraṃ bhavet..237..
2.15.d:
तस्माद्धि मुच्यते नित्यं द्वितीयं न समाचरेत्॥
यस्मिन्कर्मण्यस्य कृते मनसः स्यादलाघवम्॥
तस्मिंस्तावत्तपः कुर्याद्यावत्तुष्टिकरं भवेत्॥237॥
2.15.m: he is permanently freed from it if he does not commit it a second time. / For whatever deed has been done, if his mind feels an absence of relief, / he should perform austerity regarding it until it brings satisfaction.

2.15.s:
gurulaghutāṃ tu vicārya yathāvadyeṣu mayāgamanaṃ ca tavoktam..
teṣu na cetsahaniścitabuddhirvipravaraiḥ kuśalaiḥ sudhiyā vā..238..
2.74
puṣkara uvāca..
ityetadenasāmuktaṃ prāyaścittaṃ yathāvidhi..
ata ūrdhvaṃ rahasyānāṃ prāyaścittaṃ nibodha me..1..
pauruṣeṇa tu sūktena japyahomairdavijottamāḥ..
māsenaikena mucyante pātakaiḥ saṃyatendriyāḥ..2..
savyāhṛtīkapraṇavāḥ prāṇāyāmāstu ṣoḍaśa..
api bhrūṇahanaṃ māsātpunantyaharahaḥ kṛtāḥ ..3..
kautsaṃ japtvāpa ityetadvasiṣṭhaṃ prati ca tryṛcam..
māheśaṃ śuddhavatyaśca surāpo'pi viśudhyati..4..

haviṣmatīyamasyeti tataḥ saṃhā itīti ca ..
japtvā ca pauruṣaṃ sūktaṃ mucyate gurutalpagaḥ .. 6 ..
2.15.d:
गुरुलघुतां तु विचार्य यथावद्येषु मयागमनं च तवोक्तम्॥
तेषु न चेत्सहनिश्चितबुद्धिर्विप्रवरैः कुशलैः सुधिया वा॥238॥
2.74
पुष्कर उवाच॥
इत्येतदेनसामुक्तं प्रायश्चित्तं यथाविधि॥
अत ऊर्ध्वं रहस्यानां प्रायश्चित्तं निबोध मे॥1॥
पौरुषेण तु सूक्तेन जप्यहोमैर्दविजोत्तमाः॥
मासेनैकेन मुच्यन्ते पातकैः संयतेन्द्रियाः॥2॥
सव्याहृतीकप्रणवाः प्राणायामास्तु षोडश॥
अपि भ्रूणहनं मासात्पुनन्त्यहरहः कृताः ॥3॥
कौत्सं जप्त्वाप इत्येतद्वसिष्ठं प्रति च त्र्यृचम्॥
माहेशं शुद्धवत्यश्च सुरापोऽपि विशुध्यति॥4॥
सकृज्जप्त्वास्यवामीयं शिवसंकल्पमेव च॥
अपहृत्य सुवर्णं तु क्षणाद्भवति निर्मलः॥5॥
हविष्मतीयमस्येति ततः संहा इतीति च ॥
जप्त्वा च पौरुषं सूक्तं मुच्यते गुरुतल्पगः ॥ 6 ॥
2.15.m:
Having duly considered the gravity and lightness of those [matters] regarding which your approach has been declared by me, / if your intellect is not resolute therein, [deliberate] with eminent, skilled brahmins, or by yourself with keen discernment.
Puṣkara said: / In this manner the penance for sins has been declared according to rule. / Henceforth listen to me concerning the secret penances.
By reciting the hymn to the Cosmic Person and offering oblations into fire, the foremost twice-born, / with their senses restrained, are freed from major sins in one month.
Sixteen breath-controls accompanied by the sacred utterances and the praṇava, / performed day by day, purify even a killer of an embryo after a month.
Having recited the Kautsa hymn, the three-verse hymn to the Waters, that to Vasiṣṭha, / the hymn to Maheśa, and the Śuddhavatī verses, even a drinker of liquor is purified.
Having recited the Asyavāmīya hymn once, and likewise the Śivasaṃkalpa hymn, / a man who has stolen gold becomes pure in an instant.
Having recited the Haviṣmatīya hymn, the hymn beginning with 'asya', then 'saṃhā iti', / and the hymn to the Cosmic Person, a violator of the guru's bed is released.

2.15.s:
enasāṃ sthūlasūkṣmāṇāṃ cikīrṣannapanodanam ..
avetryṛcaṃ japedabdaṃ yatkiñcidapi tāni cet .. 7 ..
pratigṛhyāpratigṛhyaṃ bhuktvā cānnaṃ vigarhitam ..
japaṃstaratsamaṃdīyaṃ prayato mānavastryaham .. 8 ..
somāraudraṃ tu vahnīnāṃ japansatyasya śudhyati ..
sravantyāmācaretsnānaṃ paryasyamiti vā tryṛcam .. 9 ..
advā rasānamityetadenasvī saptakaṃ japet ..
aprakāśaṃ tu kṛtveno māsamāsīta bhaikṣyabhuk .. 2.74.10 ..
mantraiḥ śākalahomīyairabdaṃ hutvā ghṛtaṃ dvijaḥ ..
sugurvapyapahantyeno japtvā vāmana iṣyate .. 11 ..
drupadā nāma sā devī yajurvede pratiṣṭhitā...
antarjale trirāvṛtya mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ .. 12 ..
mahāpātakasaṃyukto na gacchedgāḥ samāhitaḥ ..
svabhyasya pāvamānīyaṃ bhaikṣyāhāro viśudhyati .. ..13..
2.15.d:
एनसां स्थूलसूक्ष्माणां चिकीर्षन्नपनोदनम् ॥
अवेत्र्यृचं जपेदब्दं यत्किञ्चिदपि तानि चेत् ॥ 7 ॥
प्रतिगृह्याप्रतिगृह्यं भुक्त्वा चान्नं विगर्हितम् ॥
जपंस्तरत्समंदीयं प्रयतो मानवस्त्र्यहम् ॥ 8 ॥
सोमारौद्रं तु वह्नीनां जपन्सत्यस्य शुध्यति ॥
स्रवन्त्यामाचरेत्स्नानं पर्यस्यमिति वा त्र्यृचम् ॥ 9 ॥
अद्वा रसानमित्येतदेनस्वी सप्तकं जपेत् ॥
अप्रकाशं तु कृत्वेनो मासमासीत भैक्ष्यभुक् ॥ 2.74.10 ॥
मन्त्रैः शाकलहोमीयैरब्दं हुत्वा घृतं द्विजः ॥
सुगुर्वप्यपहन्त्येनो जप्त्वा वामन इष्यते ॥ 11 ॥
द्रुपदा नाम सा देवी यजुर्वेदे प्रतिष्ठिता॥।
अन्तर्जले त्रिरावृत्य मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः ॥ 12 ॥
महापातकसंयुक्तो न गच्छेद्गाः समाहितः ॥
स्वभ्यस्य पावमानीयं भैक्ष्याहारो विशुध्यति ॥ ॥13॥
2.15.m:
Desiring the removal of gross and subtle sins, / if they are whatever [sins they may be], he should recite the triplet 'avet' for a year.
Having accepted an unacceptable gift and having eaten censurable food, / a restrained person reciting the Taratsamandīya hymn for three days [is purified].
Reciting the hymn to Soma and Rudra, and of the fires, he is purified of untruth; / or he should perform an ablution in a flowing river while reciting the triplet 'paryasyam'.
A sinner should recite this heptad beginning with 'advā rasānam'; / having committed a secret sin, he should subsist on begged food for a month.
Offering clarified butter for a year with the mantras of the Śākala oblations, / or having recited [them], a twice-born destroys even very grave sin; [thus] it is held.
That goddess named Drupadā, established in the Yajurveda— / repeating [her mantra] thrice while immersed in water, one is freed from all sins.
One associated with a major sin should not approach cows, [yet] remaining concentrated / and thoroughly studying the Pāvamānī hymns, living on begged food, he becomes purified.

2.15.s:
araṇye vā trirabhyasya prayato vedasaṃhitām ..
mucyate pātakaiḥ sarvaiḥ parākaiḥ śodhitastribhiḥ .. 14..
tryahaṃ tūpavasedyuktastriraho'bhyupayannapaḥ ..
mucyate pātakaiḥ sarvairjaptvā triraghamarṣaṇam .. 15 ..
yathāśvamedhaḥ sutarāṃ sarvapāpāpanodanaḥ ..
tathāghamarṣaṇaṃ sūktaṃ sarvapāpāpanodanam ..16..
hatvā lokānapīmāṃstrīnaśnannapi yatastataḥ ..
ṛgvedaṃ dhārayanvipro nainaḥ prāpnoti kiñcana..17..
ṛksaṃhitāṃ samabhyasya yajuṣāṃ vā samāhitaḥ ..
sāmnāṃ vā sarahasyānāṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate..18..
yathā mahāhradaṃ prāpya kṣipraṃ loṣṭho vinaśyati..
tathā duścaritaṃ sarvaṃ vede trivṛti majjati..19..
ṛco yajūṃṣi cādyāni sāmāni vividhāni ca ..
eṣa jñeyastrivṛdvedo yo vai veda sa vedavit ..2.74.20..
2.15.d:
अरण्ये वा त्रिरभ्यस्य प्रयतो वेदसंहिताम् ॥
मुच्यते पातकैः सर्वैः पराकैः शोधितस्त्रिभिः ॥ 14॥
त्र्यहं तूपवसेद्युक्तस्त्रिरहोऽभ्युपयन्नपः ॥
मुच्यते पातकैः सर्वैर्जप्त्वा त्रिरघमर्षणम् ॥ 15 ॥
यथाश्वमेधः सुतरां सर्वपापापनोदनः ॥
तथाघमर्षणं सूक्तं सर्वपापापनोदनम् ॥16॥
हत्वा लोकानपीमांस्त्रीनश्नन्नपि यतस्ततः ॥
ऋग्वेदं धारयन्विप्रो नैनः प्राप्नोति किञ्चन॥17॥
ऋक्संहितां समभ्यस्य यजुषां वा समाहितः ॥
साम्नां वा सरहस्यानां सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते॥18॥
यथा महाह्रदं प्राप्य क्षिप्रं लोष्ठो विनश्यति॥
तथा दुश्चरितं सर्वं वेदे त्रिवृति मज्जति॥19॥
ऋचो यजूंषि चाद्यानि सामानि विविधानि च ॥
एष ज्ञेयस्त्रिवृद्वेदो यो वै वेद स वेदवित् ॥2.74.20॥
2.15.m:
Or having studied the Saṃhitā of the Veda thrice in the wilderness, restrained, / he is freed from all sins, purified by three Parāka penances.
Disciplined, he should fast for three days, entering the water thrice a day; / having recited the Aghamarṣaṇa thrice, he is freed from all sins.
Just as the horse sacrifice completely dispels all sins, / even so the Aghamarṣaṇa hymn dispels all sins.
Even having slain these three worlds, and eating indiscriminately from anywhere, / a brahmin who retains the Ṛgveda incurs no sin whatsoever.
Having thoroughly studied the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, or that of the Yajurveda with concentration, / or that of the Sāmaveda together with the secret teachings, he is entirely freed from all sins.
Just as a lump of earth, reaching a great pool, quickly dissolves, / even so all bad conduct dissolves in the threefold Veda.
The primordial verses, sacrificial formulas, and various chants: / this is to be known as the threefold Veda; whoever knows it is truly a knower of the Veda.

2.15.s:
ādyaṃ vai tryakṣaraṃ brahma trayī yasminpratiṣṭhitā ..
sa guhyo'nyastrivṛdvedo yo vedainaṃ sa vedavit..21..

2.75
rāma uvāca ..
pretaśuddhiṃ samācakṣva sūtikāśuddhimeva ca ..
dravyaśuddhiṃ ca bhagavaṃstvaṃ hi vetsi yathātathā .. 1 ..
puṣkara uvāca ..
daśāhaṃ śāvamāśaucaṃ sapiṇḍeṣu vidhīyate ..
janane ca tathāpyevaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ bhṛgūttama .. 2 ..
dvādaśāhena rājanyaḥ pakṣādvaiśyo viśudhyati ..
māsena śuddhimāpnoti tathā śūdro'pi bhārgava .. 3 ..
2.15.d:
आद्यं वै त्र्यक्षरं ब्रह्म त्रयी यस्मिन्प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
स गुह्योऽन्यस्त्रिवृद्वेदो यो वेदैनं स वेदवित्॥21॥
वेदाभ्यासोऽन्वहं शक्त्या महायज्ञक्रियासमः॥
नाशयन्त्याशु पापानि महापातकजान्यपि ॥22॥
यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुते क्षणात्॥
तथा ज्ञानाग्निना पापं क्षिप्रं दहति वेदवित्॥23॥
ये वासुदेवं जगतामधीशं भक्त्या गताः सर्वजगत्प्रधानम् ॥
ते पातकान्याशु विधूय लोके भवन्ति चन्द्रार्कसमप्रभावाः॥24॥
2.75
राम उवाच ॥
प्रेतशुद्धिं समाचक्ष्व सूतिकाशुद्धिमेव च ॥
द्रव्यशुद्धिं च भगवंस्त्वं हि वेत्सि यथातथा ॥ 1 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
दशाहं शावमाशौचं सपिण्डेषु विधीयते ॥
जनने च तथाप्येवं ब्राह्मणानां भृगूत्तम ॥ 2 ॥
द्वादशाहेन राजन्यः पक्षाद्वैश्यो विशुध्यति ॥
मासेन शुद्धिमाप्नोति तथा शूद्रोऽपि भार्गव ॥ 3 ॥
2.15.m:
The primordial three-syllabled Brahman upon which the threefold [scripture] is founded: / that is the other, secret threefold Veda; whoever knows this is a knower of the Veda.
Daily study of the Veda to the best of one's ability, equal to the performance of the great sacrifices, / quickly destroys sins, even those born of major crimes.
Just as a kindled fire reduces fuel to ashes in an instant, / even so the knower of the Veda swiftly burns up sin with the fire of knowledge.
Those who have approached Vāsudeva with devotion, the lord of the worlds, the foremost of the whole universe, / swiftly shake off sins and become equal in splendour to the moon and the sun in the world.
Rāma said: / Declare the purification for the deceased, and also the purification for a woman in childbed, / and the purification of objects, O venerable one; for you know [them] as they truly are.
Puṣkara said: / A ten-day ritual impurity on a death is prescribed among sapiṇḍas, / and likewise at a birth, for brahmins, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
A kṣatriya becomes pure in twelve days; a vaiśya, after a fortnight; / likewise a śūdra attains purity in a month, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

2.15.s:
ānulomyena patnīnāṃ dāsīnāṃ ca bhṛgūttama ..
svāmitulyaṃ bhavecchaucaṃ mṛte svāmini yautukam .. 4 ..

brāhmaṇaḥ śuddhimāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 5 ..

2.15.d:
आनुलोम्येन पत्नीनां दासीनां च भृगूत्तम ॥
स्वामितुल्यं भवेच्छौचं मृते स्वामिनि यौतुकम् ॥ 4 ॥
षड्भिस्त्रिभिरथैकेन क्षत्रविट्शूद्रयोनिषु ॥
ब्राह्मणः शुद्धिमाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 5 ॥
विट्शूद्रयोनौ शुद्धिः स्यात्क्षत्त्रियस्य तथैव च ॥
षड्रात्रेण त्रिरात्रेण षड्भिः शूद्रस्तथा विशः ॥6 ॥
अदन्तजातबाले तु सद्यः शौचं विधीयते ॥
बाले त्वकृतचूडे च विशुद्धिर्नैशिकी स्मृता ॥ 7 ॥
तथा चानुपनीते तु त्रिरात्राच्छुद्धिरिष्यते ॥
ततः परं दशाहेन शुद्धेयुस्तस्य बान्धवाः॥8॥
ऊनत्रिवार्षिके शुद्धे पञ्चाहा शुद्धिरिष्यते ॥
द्वादशाहेन शुद्धिः स्यादतीते वत्सरत्रये॥9॥
गतैः संवत्सरैः षड्भिः शुद्धिर्मासेन कीर्तिता॥
स्त्रीणामकृतचूडानां विशुद्धिर्नैशिकी स्मृता॥2.75.10॥
2.15.m:
In the direct order of castes for wives and female slaves, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / their purity upon the death of the master is equal to the master's, as a combined rule.
A brahmin attains purity in six, three, or one [day] / regarding [relatives born of] kṣatriya, vaiśya, and śūdra wombs; no doubt should be entertained on this.
For a kṣatriya, purity regarding a vaiśya and śūdra womb would likewise be / in six nights and three nights [respectively]; a vaiśya regarding a śūdra, likewise in six [nights].
In the case of a child whose teeth have not appeared, immediate purity is prescribed; / but in the case of a child whose tonsure has not been performed, purification lasting one night is taught.
And likewise for an uninitiated [child], purification is held to occur after three nights; / after that, his relatives would become pure in ten days.
For a pure [child] under three years old, purification is held to be five days; / purification would be in twelve days when three years have passed.
When six years have passed, purification is proclaimed to be in a month; / for females whose tonsure has not been performed, purification lasting one night is taught.

2.15.s:

2.15.d:
तथा हि कृतचूडानां त्र्यहाच्छुध्यन्ति बान्धवाः ॥
विवाहितासु नाशौचं पितृपक्षे विधीयते ॥ 11 ॥
पितृगृहे प्रसूतायां विशुद्धिर्नैशिकी स्मृता ॥
सूतिका दशरात्रेण शुद्धिमाप्नोति नान्यथा ॥ 12 ॥।
विवाहिताऽपि चेत्कन्या म्रियते पितृवेश्मनि ॥
तस्यास्त्रिरात्राच्छुध्यन्ति बान्धवा नात्र संशयः ॥ 13॥
पितृवेश्मनि या कन्या रजः पश्यत्यसंस्कृता ॥
तस्यां मृतायां नाशौचं कदाचिदपि शाम्यति ॥ 14 ॥
सस्नानं खलु शौचं च प्रथमेन समापयेत् ॥
असमानं द्वितीयेन धर्मराजवचो यथा ॥ 19 ॥
देशान्तरस्थाः श्रुत्वा तु कुल्यानां मरणोद्भवौ ॥
यच्छेषं दशरात्रस्य तावदेव शुचिर्भवेत् ॥ 16 ॥
अतीते दशरात्रे तु त्रिरात्रमशुचिर्भवेत्॥
तथा संवत्सरेऽतीते स्नात एव च शुद्ध्यति ॥ 17 ॥
मातामहे तथातीते आचार्ये च तथा मृते ॥
अनौरसेषु पुत्रेषु भार्यास्वन्यगतासु च ॥ 18 ॥
2.15.m:
For those whose tonsure has been performed, the relatives become pure after three days; / for married women, no ritual impurity is prescribed on the father's side.
When [a child] is delivered in the father's house, purification lasting one night is taught; / the woman in childbed attains purity in ten nights, not otherwise.
If a girl, even though married, dies in her father's house, / her relatives become pure after three nights; of this there is no doubt.
If an unmarried girl sees her menstrual blood in her father's house, / when she dies, the ritual impurity never ceases.
One should conclude purity with bathing by the first [period of impurity], / [if the second is] not equal to the second, as is the saying of the King of Dharma.
Those staying in another land, having heard of the death or birth of family members, / shall be pure for just as much as remains of the ten nights.
When the ten nights have passed, one would be impure for three nights; / likewise when a year has passed, one is purified simply by bathing.
Likewise when a maternal grandfather has passed away, and likewise when a teacher has died, / and in the case of non-legitimate sons, and wives who have gone to another,

nivāse rājani prete mātule śvaśure tathā .. 19 ..
ācāryapatnīputreṣu śiṣye sabrahmacāriṇi ..

2.15.d:
परपूर्वासु भार्यासु त्रिरात्राच्छुद्धिरिष्यते ॥
निवासे राजनि प्रेते मातुले श्वशुरे तथा ॥ 19 ॥
आचार्यपत्नीपुत्रेषु शिष्ये सब्रह्मचारिणि ॥
एकरात्रमशौचं स्यादन्नदाने तथा मृते ॥ 2.75.20 ॥
रात्रिभिर्मासतुल्याभिर्गर्भस्रावे विशोधनम् ॥
सपिण्डे ब्राह्मणे वर्णाः सर्व एवाविशेषतः ॥ 21 ॥
दशरात्रेण शुद्धयन्ति द्वादशाहेन भूमिपाः ॥
वैश्यः पञ्चदशाहेन शूद्रो मासेन भार्गव ॥22॥
भृग्वग्न्यनाशनांभोभिर्मृतानामात्मघातिनाम् ॥
पतितानां च नाशौचं विद्युच्छस्त्रहताश्च ये ॥ 23 ॥
सती व्रती ब्रह्मचारी नृपकारकदीक्षिताः ॥
नाशौचभाजः कथिता राजकार्यकराश्च ये ॥24॥
अनुगम्येच्छया प्रेतं ज्ञातिमज्ञातिमेव वा ॥
सवासा जलमाप्लुत्य घृतं प्राश्य विशुध्यति॥
मैथुने कटधूमे च सद्यः स्नानं विधीयते ॥ 25॥
2.15.m:
and in the case of wives who belonged previously to another, purification is held to be after three nights; / when the king of the country of residence is deceased, likewise for a maternal uncle, a father-in-law,
for the wife and sons of a teacher, a pupil, and a fellow student, / ritual impurity shall last one night; likewise on the death of one who provides food.
In the case of a miscarriage, purification is in nights equal to the months [of pregnancy]; / for a brahmin sapiṇḍa, all castes without distinction
become pure in ten nights; rulers of the earth, in twelve days; / a vaiśya in fifteen days, and a śūdra in a month, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
For those who die by falling from a cliff, by fire, by fasting, or in water, suicides, / and outcasts, there is no ritual impurity; nor for those who are killed by lightning or a weapon.
A virtuous wife, one observing a vow, a religious student, those consecrated for royal rituals, / and those carrying out the king's business are declared not to partake of ritual impurity.
Voluntarily following a deceased relative or non-relative, / bathing in water with one's clothes on and consuming clarified butter, one becomes purified; / upon sexual intercourse and the smoke of a funeral pyre, immediate bathing is prescribed.

2.15.s:
jananamaraṇayoḥ śucirdaśāhena bhavati śaucavidherna viprayojyam ..
na ca bhavati pratigraheṣu doṣo dvipada catuṣpadadhānyadakṣiṇāsu..26..
2.15.d:
जननमरणयोः शुचिर्दशाहेन भवति शौचविधेर्न विप्रयोज्यम् ॥
न च भवति प्रतिग्रहेषु दोषो द्विपद चतुष्पदधान्यदक्षिणासु॥26॥
2.15.m: In birth and death, one becomes pure in ten days; one should not separate from the rule of purity; / nor does any fault arise in the acceptance of gifts consisting of bipeds, quadrupeds, grain, and sacrificial fees.

2.16.s:

dvijaṃ na nirharetpretaṃ śūdreṇa tu kathaṃcana .
na ca śūdraṃ dvijenāpi tayordoṣo'bhijāyate .. 1 ..

पुष्कर उवाच ।
द्विजं न निर्हरेत्प्रेतं शूद्रेण तु कथंचन ।
न च शूद्रं द्विजेनापि तयोर्दोषोऽभिजायते ॥ 1 ॥
2.16.m:
Puṣkara said:
A deceased twice-born must never be carried out by a śūdra, / nor a śūdra by a twice-born; a fault is born to both of them.

2.16.s:
anāthaṃ brāhmaṇapretaṃ ye vahanti dvijātayaḥ .
padepade kratuphalaṃ cānupūrvāllabhanti te..2..
2.16.d:
अनाथं ब्राह्मणप्रेतं ये वहन्ति द्विजातयः ।
पदेपदे क्रतुफलं चानुपूर्वाल्लभन्ति ते॥2॥
2.16.m: Those twice-born who carry a destitute deceased brahmin / obtain the fruit of a sacrifice at every step in due succession.

2.16.s:
saṃskārārthamanāthasya yastu kāṣṭhaṃ prayacchati ..
kāṣṭhāgnidātā prākāśyaṃ saṃgrāme labhate jayam ..3..
2.16.d:
संस्कारार्थमनाथस्य यस्तु काष्ठं प्रयच्छति ॥
काष्ठाग्निदाता प्राकाश्यं संग्रामे लभते जयम् ॥3॥
2.16.m: He who offers wood for the sacrament of a destitute person, / that giver of wood and fire attains renown and victory in battle.

2.16.s:
saṃjvālya bāndhavaṃ pretamapasavyena tāṃ citim ..
parikramya tataḥ snānaṃ kuryuḥ sarve svabāndhavāḥ ..4..
2.16.d:
संज्वाल्य बान्धवं प्रेतमपसव्येन तां चितिम् ॥
परिक्रम्य ततः स्नानं कुर्युः सर्वे स्वबान्धवाः ॥4॥
2.16.m: Having cremated the deceased relative and circumambulated that pyre / from right to left, all the relatives should then bathe.

2.16.s:
pretāya ca tathā dadyustisro vai codakāñjalīḥ ..
dvāryaśmani padaṃ dattvā praviśeyustathā gṛham .. ..5..
2.16.d:
प्रेताय च तथा दद्युस्तिस्रो वै चोदकाञ्जलीः ॥
द्वार्यश्मनि पदं दत्त्वा प्रविशेयुस्तथा गृहम् ॥ ॥5॥
2.16.m: And they should offer three handfuls of water to the deceased; / having placed a foot on a stone at the doorway, they should then enter the house.

2.16.s:
akṣatā nikṣipeyuśca tathā vahnau samāhitāḥ ..
vidaśya nimbapatrāṇi śayīraṃśca pṛthak kṣitau..6..
2.16.d:
अक्षता निक्षिपेयुश्च तथा वह्नौ समाहिताः ॥
विदश्य निम्बपत्राणि शयीरंश्च पृथक् क्षितौ॥6॥
2.16.m: And, concentrated in mind, they should cast unbroken grains of rice into the fire; / having chewed leaves of the neem tree, they should sleep separately on the ground.

2.16.s:
krītalabdhāśanāścaiva bhaveyuḥ susamāhitāḥ ..
na caiva māṃsamaśnīyurvrajeyurna ca yoṣitam .. 7 ..
2.16.d:
क्रीतलब्धाशनाश्चैव भवेयुः सुसमाहिताः ॥
न चैव मांसमश्नीयुर्व्रजेयुर्न च योषितम् ॥ 7 ॥
2.16.m: And, well-composed, their food should be bought or received [from others]; / they must not eat meat, nor go to a woman.

2.16.s:
nivartayeyustathaivaikaṃ piṇḍaṃ pretasya nityadā ..
aśaucaṃ yāvadeva syāttasminvyapagate punaḥ ..8..
2.16.d:
निवर्तयेयुस्तथैवैकं पिण्डं प्रेतस्य नित्यदा ॥
अशौचं यावदेव स्यात्तस्मिन्व्यपगते पुनः ॥8॥
2.16.m: In the very same way, they should constantly offer one rice-ball to the deceased / for as long as the ritual impurity lasts; when that has passed, however,

2.16.s:
śmaśrukarma tadā kṛtvā snātāḥ siddhārthakaistilaiḥ ..
pūjayeyurdvijānrāma parivartitavāsasaḥ ..9..
2.16.d:
श्मश्रुकर्म तदा कृत्वा स्नाताः सिद्धार्थकैस्तिलैः ॥
पूजयेयुर्द्विजान्राम परिवर्तितवाससः ॥9॥
2.16.m: having then shaved, bathed with white mustard seeds and sesame seeds, / and changed their clothes, O Rāma, they should honor the twice-born.

2.16.s:
adantajātestanaye śiśau garbhacyute tathā ..
kāryo naivā'gnisaṃskāro naiva cāsyodakakriyā ..2.76.10..
2.16.d:
अदन्तजातेस्तनये शिशौ गर्भच्युते तथा ॥
कार्यो नैवाऽग्निसंस्कारो नैव चास्योदकक्रिया ॥2.76.10॥
2.16.m: For a child whose teeth have not erupted, and likewise for an infant miscarried from the womb, / the sacrament of fire must not be performed, nor the rite of water for him.

2.16.s:
caturthe ca dine kāryaścaivāsthnāṃ rāma saṃcayaḥ ..
asthisaṃcayanādūrdhvaṃ kulasparśo vidhīyate .. 11 ..
2.16.d:
चतुर्थे च दिने कार्यश्चैवास्थ्नां राम संचयः ॥
अस्थिसंचयनादूर्ध्वं कुलस्पर्शो विधीयते ॥ 11 ॥
2.16.m: And on the fourth day, O Rāma, the gathering of the bones should be performed; / after the gathering of the bones, touching one's kin is prescribed.

2.16.s:
mṛtasya bāndhavaiḥ sārdhaṃ kṛtvāśrupatanaṃ naraḥ ..
asthisaṃcayanādarvāk sacailaṃ snānamācaret ..12..
2.16.d:
मृतस्य बान्धवैः सार्धं कृत्वाश्रुपतनं नरः ॥
अस्थिसंचयनादर्वाक् सचैलं स्नानमाचरेत् ॥12॥
2.16.m: A man who sheds tears along with the relatives of the dead / must take a bath with his clothes on before the gathering of the bones.

2.16.s:
snātaśca śuddhimāpnoti tataḥ paramiti śrutiḥ ..
asthnāṃ gaṅgāmbhasi kṣepātpretasyābhyudayo bhavet .. 13 ..
2.16.d:
स्नातश्च शुद्धिमाप्नोति ततः परमिति श्रुतिः ॥
अस्थ्नां गङ्गाम्भसि क्षेपात्प्रेतस्याभ्युदयो भवेत् ॥ 13 ॥
2.16.m: And once bathed he attains purity, but beyond that [gathering] is revealed [different rule]; / from casting the bones into the water of the Gaṅgā, the deceased attains elevation.

2.16.s:
asthnāṃ hi plāvanārthāya sāgarāṇāṃ mahātmanām ..
gaganādbhuvamānītā gaṅgā gaganamekhalā .. 14 ..
2.16.d:
अस्थ्नां हि प्लावनार्थाय सागराणां महात्मनाम् ॥
गगनाद्भुवमानीता गङ्गा गगनमेखला ॥ 14 ॥
2.16.m: For in order to submerge the bones of the great-souled sons of Sagara, / the Gaṅgā, the celestial girdle, was brought down to earth from the sky

2.16.s:
bhagīrathena dharmajña tapasā mahatā purā ..
sagarasya sutāḥ sarve narakasthā bhṛgūttama .. 15 ..
2.16.d:
भगीरथेन धर्मज्ञ तपसा महता पुरा ॥
सगरस्य सुताः सर्वे नरकस्था भृगूत्तम ॥ 15 ॥
2.16.m: in ancient times by Bhagīratha through great austerity, O knower of dharma; / all the sons of Sagara residing in hell, O foremost of the Bhṛgus,

2.16.s:
gaṅgātoyāplutā rāma divamakṣayyamāgatāḥ ..
gaṅgātoyena yasyāsthi yāvatsaṃkhyaṃ nimajjati .. 16 ..
2.16.d:
गङ्गातोयाप्लुता राम दिवमक्षय्यमागताः ॥
गङ्गातोयेन यस्यास्थि यावत्संख्यं निमज्जति ॥ 16 ॥
2.16.m: bathed in the water of the Gaṅgā, O Rāma, reached imperishable heaven; / for as many [particles] of a person’s bone sink in the water of the Gaṅgā,

2.16.s:
tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi svargaloke mahīyate ..
ātmanastyāgināṃ nāsti patitānāṃ tathā kriyā .. 17 ..
2.16.d:
तावद्वर्षसहस्राणि स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥
आत्मनस्त्यागिनां नास्ति पतितानां तथा क्रिया ॥ 17 ॥
2.16.m: for that many thousands of years he is exalted in the heavenly world; / there is no [such] rite for those who take their own lives or for outcasts.

2.16.s:
teṣāmapi tathā gaṅgātoye syātpatanaṃ hitam ..
patitānāṃ tu yaddattaṃ śrāddhaṃ cātha jalāñjaliḥ .. 18 ..
2.16.d:
तेषामपि तथा गङ्गातोये स्यात्पतनं हितम् ॥
पतितानां तु यद्दत्तं श्राद्धं चाथ जलाञ्जलिः ॥ 18 ॥
2.16.m: Even for them, falling into the water of the Gaṅgā is beneficial; / but whatever ancestral offering or handful of water is offered for outcasts,

2.16.s:
na tatpretaḥ samāpnoti gagane pravilīyate ..
anugraheṇa sahitā pretasya patitasya tu .. 19 ..

2.16.m:
Hari, the great soul of immeasurable strength and valor, endowed with great splendor, removes adversity and fear; / when worshipped by people stained with hundreds of sins, Vāsudeva leads them to heaven.
Puṣkara said:
When ritual impurity has elapsed, having bathed with a restrained mind, / [one should seat] twice-born who have bathed, are adorned, shining with perfume and garments, with devotion,
and feed them facing north, well seated and concentrated; / here, modifications of mantras should also be made, and in the singular.
Near the food leftovers, one should place one rice-ball, / and, concentrated, pronounce his name and lineage.
When the brahmins have eaten and have been honored with wealth, / and water for inexhaustible merit has been poured out along with the recitation of name and lineage,
one should make three trenches, four finger-widths in width, / dug out to that same depth, and a span in length.
Near the trenches, he should kindle three fires; / concentrated, O Rāma, to Soma, to Agni, and to Yama,

जुहुयादाहुतीः सम्यक् तथैव च त्रयस्त्रयः ॥
पिण्डनिर्वपणं कुर्यात्प्राग्वदेव पृथक्पृथक् ॥ 7 ॥
अन्नेन दध्ना मधुना तथा मांसेन पूरयेत् ॥
मध्ये चेदधिवासः स्यात्कुर्यादभ्यधिकं ततः ॥ 8 ॥
अथवा द्वादशाहेन सर्वमेतत्समापयेत् ॥
संवत्सरस्य मध्ये चेद्यदि स्यादधिमासकः ॥ 9 ॥
ततो द्वादशके श्राद्धे कार्यं तदधिमासिकम् ॥
ततो द्वादशके श्राद्धे कार्यं तदधिकं भवेत्॥2.77.10॥
संवत्सरे समाप्ते तु श्राद्धं श्राद्धवदाचरेत् ॥
प्रेताय तस्मादूर्ध्वं च तस्यैव पुरुषत्रये ॥ 11 ॥
पिण्डान्विनिर्वपेच्चात्र चतुरः सुसमाहितः ॥
संसृजं पृथिवीं दत्त्वा समानावेति चाप्यथ ॥ 12 ॥
योजयेत्प्रेतपिण्डं तु पिण्डेष्वन्येषु भार्गव ॥
प्रेतपात्रं च पात्रेषु तथैव विनियोजयेत् ॥13॥
2.16.m:
he should properly pour oblations, three each in the same way; / he should perform the offering of rice-balls individually, just as before.
He should fill [the trenches] with boiled rice, curd, honey, and meat; / if an intercalary month occurs in the middle, he should subsequently perform an additional [offering].
Or else he should complete all this in twelve days; / and if there should be an intercalary month within the year,
then in the twelfth ancestral offering, that intercalary rite must be performed; / then in the twelfth ancestral offering, it should be an extra rite.
When the year is completed, he should perform an ancestral offering according to the rules of ancestral offerings; / thereafter, for the deceased, and for his three ancestors,
he should, well concentrated, cast down four rice-balls here; / having placed [them] together reciting “O Earth!” and then “Equal are…,”
he should join the rice-ball of the deceased with the other rice-balls, O Bhārgava, / and similarly join the vessel of the deceased with the vessels.

यावज्जीवं तथा कुर्याच्छ्राद्धं तु प्रतिवत्सरम् ॥

पुष्कर उवाच ॥

नित्यमस्मिन्निरालम्बे काले सततयायिनि ॥
न तद्भूतं प्रपस्यामि स्थितिर्यस्य भवेद्ध्रुवा ॥ 2 ॥
गङ्गायाः सिकताधारास्तथा वर्षति वासवे ॥
शक्या गणयितुं लोके न व्यतीताः पितामहाः ॥ 3 ॥
2.16.m:
This rite should be performed separately for each of the three rituals; / this rite without mantras is prescribed also for a śūdra.
This should likewise be performed for women without the recitation of mantras; / and as long as one lives, one should perform an ancestral offering every year / by this very procedure, with devotion and a restrained mind.
Food along with a jar of water should be given daily with devotion for the deceased until the end of the year; / this must be done by the relatives; grief should not be indulged, for one who grieves can accomplish nothing at all.
Puṣkara said:
Those whose relatives have died should be consoled by wise relatives / with words full of dharma; hear those and others from me.
In this continuously moving time, which is ever without support, / I see no living being whose staying could be permanent.
The grains of sand in the Gaṅgā, and likewise [the drops] when Indra rains, / can be counted in the world, but not the grandfathers who have passed away.

चतुर्दश विनश्यन्ति कल्पेकल्पे सुरेश्वराः ॥
सर्वलोकप्रधानाश्च मनवश्च चतुर्दश ॥ 4 ॥
बहूनीन्द्रसहस्राणि दैत्येन्द्रनियुतानि च ॥
विनष्टानीह कालेन मनुजेष्वथ का कथा ॥ 5 ॥
राजर्षयश्च बहवः सर्वे समुदिता गुणैः ॥
देवा ब्रह्मर्षयश्चैव कालेन निधनं गताः ॥ 6 ॥
ये समर्था जगत्यस्मिन्सृष्टिसंहारकारणे॥
तेऽपि कालेन नीयन्ते कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः॥7॥
आक्रम्य सर्वं कालेन परलोकाय नीयते ॥
कर्म पश्यति नो जन्तुस्तत्र का परिदेवना ॥8॥
जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च ॥
अस्मिन्दुष्परिहार्येऽर्थे नास्ति लोके सहायता ॥ 9 ॥
शोचन्तो नोपकुर्वन्ति मृतस्य हि जना यदा ॥
अतो न शोचितव्यं स्यात्क्रिया कार्या सुयत्नतः ॥ 2.78.10 ॥
सुकृतं दुष्कृतं चोभौ सहायौ यस्य गच्छतः ॥
बान्धवैस्तस्य किं कार्यं शोचद्भिरथ वा न वा ॥ 11 ॥
2.16.m:
In every kalpa, fourteen lords of gods perish, / and fourteen Manus, the foremost of all the worlds.
Many thousands of Indras and hundreds of thousands of lords of Daityas / have been destroyed here by time; what then of human beings?
And many royal sages, all rich in virtues, / gods, and divine sages have gone to their death through time.
Even those who are capable of creating and destroying this universe / are borne away by time; for time is insurmountable.
Assailing everything, time bears it away to the other world; / a living creature sees only [its own] karma. What cause is there for lamentation?
For to what is born, death is certain, and birth is certain to what has died; / in this unavoidable matter, there is no helper in the world.
Since people do not help the deceased by grieving, / therefore one should not grieve; the ritual must be performed with great care.
Both good deeds and bad deeds go with him as companions; / what can relatives do for him, whether grieving or not?

बान्धवानामशौचे तु स्थितिं प्रेतो न विन्दति ॥
अतस्त्वभ्येति तानेव पिण्डतोयप्रदायिनः ॥ 12 ॥
अर्वाक् सपिण्डीकरणात्प्रेतो भवति यो मृतः ॥
प्रेतलोकगतस्यान्नं सोदकुम्भं प्रयच्छत ॥ 13 ॥
पितृलोकगतश्चान्नं श्राद्धं भुङ्क्ते सुधासमम् ॥
पितृलोकगतस्यास्य तस्माच्छ्राद्धं प्रयत्नतः ॥ 14 ॥
देवत्वे यातनास्थाने तिर्यग्योनौ तथैव च ॥
मानुष्ये च तथाऽप्नोति श्राद्धे दत्ते स्वबान्धवैः ॥ 15॥
प्रेतस्य श्राद्धकर्तुश्च पुष्टिः श्राद्धे कृते ध्रुवम् ॥
तस्माच्छ्राद्धं सदा कार्यं शोकं त्यक्त्वा निरर्थकम् ॥16॥
एतावदेव कर्तव्यं सदा प्रेतस्य बन्धुभिः॥
नोपकुर्यान्नरः शोचन्प्रेतस्यात्मन एव च॥17॥
दृष्ट्वा लोकमनाक्रन्दं म्रियमाणांश्च बान्धवान् ॥
धर्ममेकं सहायार्थे कारयध्वं सदा नराः ॥ 18॥
2.16.m:
During the ritual impurity of relatives, the deceased finds no resting place; / therefore he approaches those very persons who offer balls of rice and water.
A dead person remains a deceased [spirit] before the sapiṇḍa ritual; / offer food together with a water jar to him who has gone to the world of the deceased.
And having gone to the world of the ancestors, he consumes the food of the śrāddha like nectar; / therefore, a śrāddha [must be performed] with effort for one who has gone to the world of the ancestors.
Whether in divine state, in a place of torment, in an animal womb, / or in human state, he attains it when a śrāddha is offered by his own relatives.
Nourishment is assured for the deceased and for the performer of the śrāddha when the śrāddha is performed; / therefore a śrāddha must always be performed, casting aside useless grief.
This much alone should always be done by the kin of the deceased; / by grieving, a person helps neither the deceased nor himself.
Seeing the world without shelter and relatives dying, / O men, always practice dharma alone as a companion!

śvaḥ kāryamadya kurvīta pūrvāhṇe tvaparāhṇikam ..
na hi pratīkṣate mṛtyuḥ kṛtamasya na vā kṛtama .. 21 ..
kṣetrāpaṇagṛhāsaktamanyatra gatamānasam ..
vṛkīvā'raṇyamāsādya mṛtyurādāya gacchati..22..
na kālasya priyaḥ kaścidveṣyaścāsya na vidyate ..
āyuṣye karmaṇi kṣīṇe prasahya harate janam..23..
2.16.d:
मृतोऽपि बान्धवः शक्तो नानुगन्तुं नरैर्यतः ॥
जायावर्ज्यं हि सर्वस्य यस्या भर्ता विभिद्यते ॥ 19 ॥
धर्म एकोऽनुयात्येनं यत्र कुत्र च गामिनम् ॥
नन्वसारे त्रिलोके ऽस्मिन्धर्म कुरु मा चिरम् ॥ 2.78.20 ॥
श्वः कार्यमद्य कुर्वीत पूर्वाह्णे त्वपराह्णिकम् ॥
न हि प्रतीक्षते मृत्युः कृतमस्य न वा कृतम ॥ 21 ॥
क्षेत्रापणगृहासक्तमन्यत्र गतमानसम् ॥
वृकीवाऽरण्यमासाद्य मृत्युरादाय गच्छति॥22॥
न कालस्य प्रियः कश्चिद्वेष्यश्चास्य न विद्यते ॥
आयुष्ये कर्मणि क्षीणे प्रसह्य हरते जनम्॥23॥
2.16.m:
Because even a dead relative cannot be followed by people— / with the sole exception of a wife, whose husband is divided [from her].
Dharma alone follows him wherever he goes; / truly, in this worthless threefold world, practice dharma without delay!
What is to be done tomorrow, one should do today, and what is of the afternoon, in the forenoon; / for death does not wait [to see] whether his work is done or not done.
Attached to fields, shops, and homes, with his mind directed elsewhere, / death seizes him and departs, like a she-wolf entering a forest.
Time has no one dear, nor is anyone hated by it; / when the karma of lifespan is exhausted, it forcibly carries off a person.

2.16.s:
nāprāptakālo mriyate viddhaḥ śaraśatairapi ..
kuśāgreṇāpi saṃspṛṣṭaḥ prāptakālo na jīvati ..24..
2.16.d:
नाप्राप्तकालो म्रियते विद्धः शरशतैरपि ॥
कुशाग्रेणापि संस्पृष्टः प्राप्तकालो न जीवति ॥24॥
2.16.m: One whose time has not arrived does not die, even when pierced by a hundred arrows; / one whose time has arrived does not live, even when merely touched by the tip of a kuśa grass blade.

2.16.s:
nauṣadhāni na mantrāśca na homā na punarjapāḥ ..
trāyante mṛtyunopetaṃ jarayā vāpi mānavam..25..
2.16.d:
नौषधानि न मन्त्राश्च न होमा न पुनर्जपाः ॥
त्रायन्ते मृत्युनोपेतं जरया वापि मानवम्॥25॥
2.16.m: Neither medicines, nor mantras, nor burnt offerings, nor repeated prayers / protect a human being approached by death or old age.

2.16.s:
āgāminamanarthaṃ tu pratighātaśatairapi ..
na nivārayituṃ śaktāstatra kā paridevanā ..26..
2.16.d:
आगामिनमनर्थं तु प्रतिघातशतैरपि ॥
न निवारयितुं शक्तास्तत्र का परिदेवना ॥26॥
2.16.m: They are not able to ward off impending misfortune even with hundreds of obstacles; / what cause is there for lamentation?

2.16.s:
yathā dhenusahasreṣu vatso vindati mātaram ..
tathā pūrvakṛtaṃ karma kartāraṃ vindate dhruvam ...27..
2.16.d:
यथा धेनुसहस्रेषु वत्सो विन्दति मातरम् ॥
तथा पूर्वकृतं कर्म कर्तारं विन्दते ध्रुवम् ॥.27॥
2.16.m: Just as a calf finds its mother among a thousand cows, / so previously performed karma certainly finds its doer.

2.16.s:
avyaktādīni sarvāṇi vyaktamadhyāni cāpyatha ..
avyaktanidhanānyeva tatra kā paridevanā ..28..
2.16.d:
अव्यक्तादीनि सर्वाणि व्यक्तमध्यानि चाप्यथ ॥
अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना ॥28॥
2.16.m: All beings have an unmanifest beginning, a manifest middle, / and an unmanifest end; what cause is there for lamentation?

2.16.s:
dehinosminyathā dehaṃ kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā ..
tathā janmāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati .. 29 ..
2.16.d:
देहिनोस्मिन्यथा देहं कौमारं यौवनं जरा ॥
तथा जन्मान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥ 29 ॥
2.16.m: Just as the embodied [soul] experiences in this body childhood, youth, and old age, / so does it attain another birth; the wise person is not bewildered by that.

2.16.s:
gṛhṇātīva yathā vastraṃ tyaktvā pūrvadhṛtaṃ naraḥ..
gṛhṇātyevaṃ navaṃ dehaṃ dehīkarmanibandhanaḥ..2.78.30..
2.16.d:
गृह्णातीव यथा वस्त्रं त्यक्त्वा पूर्वधृतं नरः॥
गृह्णात्येवं नवं देहं देहीकर्मनिबन्धनः॥2.78.30॥
2.16.m: Just as a man casts off previously worn clothing and takes another, / so the embodied [soul], bound by karma, takes a new body.

2.16.s:
nainaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ ..
na cainaṃ kledayantyāpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ .. 31 ..
2.16.d:
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः ॥
न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः ॥ 31 ॥
2.16.m: Weapons do not cut this [soul], fire does not burn it, / waters do not wet it, and the wind does not dry it.

2.16.s:
acchedyo'yamadāhyo'yamakledyo'śoṣya eva ca ..
nityaḥ sarvagataḥsthāṇuracalo'yaṃ sanātanaḥ..32..
2.16.d:
अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च ॥
नित्यः सर्वगतःस्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः॥32॥
2.16.m: This cannot be cut, this cannot be burned, it cannot be wetted or dried; / it is eternal, all-pervading, stable, immovable, and primeval.

2.16.s:
avyakto'yamacintyo'yamavikāryo'yameva ca ..
tasmādevaṃ vidittvainaṃ nānuśocitumarhatha .. 33 ..
2.16.d:
अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमेव च ॥
तस्मादेवं विदित्त्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हथ ॥ 33 ॥
2.16.m: This is unmanifest, this is unthinkable, and this is immutable; / therefore, knowing it thus, you should not grieve.

2.16.s:
āścaryavatpaśyati kaścidenamāścaryavadvadati tathaiva cānyaḥ ..
āścaryavaścainamanyaḥ śṛṇoti śrutvāpyenaṃ veda na caiva kaścit ..34...
2.79
.. puṣkara uvāca . .
mṛnmayaṃ bhājanaṃ sarvaṃ punaḥ pākena śudhyati ..
madyairmūtrapurīṣairvā ṣṭhīvanaiḥ pūyaśoṇitaiḥ..1..
saṃspṛṣṭaṃ naiva śudhyeta punaḥpākena mṛnmayam ..
etaireva tathā spṛṣṭaṃ tāmrasauvarṇarājatam..2..
śudhyatyātāpitaṃ paścādanyathā kevalāmbhasā..
amlodakena tāmrasya sīsasya trapusastathā..3..
kṣāreṇa śuddhiṃ kāṃsyasya lohasya ca vinirdiśet..
muktāmaṇipravālānāṃ śuddhiḥ prakṣālanena tu..4..
anyeṣāṃ caiva bhāṇḍānāṃ sarvasyāśmamayasya ca ..
śākarajjumūlaphalavaidalānāṃ tathaiva ca..5..
mārjanādyajñabhāṇḍānāṃ pāṇinā cāgnikarmaṇi ..
uṣṇāmbhasā tathā śuddhiḥ sasnehānāṃ vinirdiśet .. 6 ..
2.16.d:
आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेनमाश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः ॥
आश्चर्यवश्चैनमन्यः शृणोति श्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित् ॥34॥।
2.79
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥
मृन्मयं भाजनं सर्वं पुनः पाकेन शुध्यति ॥
मद्यैर्मूत्रपुरीषैर्वा ष्ठीवनैः पूयशोणितैः॥1॥
संस्पृष्टं नैव शुध्येत पुनःपाकेन मृन्मयम् ॥
एतैरेव तथा स्पृष्टं ताम्रसौवर्णराजतम्॥2॥
शुध्यत्यातापितं पश्चादन्यथा केवलाम्भसा॥
अम्लोदकेन ताम्रस्य सीसस्य त्रपुसस्तथा॥3॥
क्षारेण शुद्धिं कांस्यस्य लोहस्य च विनिर्दिशेत्॥
मुक्तामणिप्रवालानां शुद्धिः प्रक्षालनेन तु॥4॥
अन्येषां चैव भाण्डानां सर्वस्याश्ममयस्य च ॥
शाकरज्जुमूलफलवैदलानां तथैव च॥5॥
मार्जनाद्यज्ञभाण्डानां पाणिना चाग्निकर्मणि ॥
उष्णाम्भसा तथा शुद्धिः सस्नेहानां विनिर्दिशेत् ॥ 6 ॥
2.16.m:
One looks upon this as a wonder; likewise another speaks of it as a wonder; / another hears of it as a wonder; and even having heard of it, no one knows it.
Puṣkara said: / Every clay vessel is purified by re-firing. / [When] defiled by liquor, urine, or feces, or by spittle, pus, and blood,
an earthenware [vessel] that has been touched is not purified even by re-firing. / When touched by these very same [substances], copper, gold, and silver
are purified by being heated [in fire]; otherwise, [they are purified] with water alone; / of copper, lead, and tin, with acidic water;
one should prescribe purification with alkaline ashes for bronze and iron; / but the purification of pearls, gems, and corals is by washing.
And of other vessels, and of everything made of stone, / as well as of vegetables, ropes, roots, fruits, and split-bamboo items,
and of sacrificial vessels, [purification is] by wiping with the hand during the rite of fire. / Likewise, one should prescribe the purification of oily objects with hot water.

2.16.s:
śayanāsanayānānāṃ sphyaśūrpaśakaṭasya ca ..
śuddhiḥ saṃkṣepaṇājjñeyā palālendhanayostathā .. 7 ..
mārjanādveśmanāṃ śuddhiḥ kṣitau śodhanataḥ kṣaṇāt ..
saṃmārjitena toyena vāsasāṃ śuddhiriṣyate .. .. 8 ..
bahūnāṃ prokṣaṇācchuddhiḥ dhānyānāṃ ca vinirdiśet ..
śuddhirdrumāṇā vijñeyā nityasatpavanena tu .. 9 ..
prokṣaṇātsaṃhatānāṃ tu dāravāṇāṃ ca takṣaṇāt ..
siddhārthakāṇāṃ kalkena śṛṅgadantamayasya ca .. 2.79.10 ..
govālaiḥ phalapatrāṇāmasthnāṃ syācchṛṅgavastathā ..
niryāsānāṃ guḍānāṃ ca lavaṇānāṃ tathaiva ca .. 11 ..
kusumbhakuṃkumānāṃ ca ūrṇākārpāsayostathā ..
prokṣaṇātkathitā śuddhirityāha bhagavān hi saḥ .. 12 ..
bhūmiṣṭhamudakaṃ śuddhaṃ tathaiva ca śilāgatam ..
varṇagandharasairduṣṭairvarjitaṃ yadi tadbhavet .. 13 ..
2.16.d:
शयनासनयानानां स्फ्यशूर्पशकटस्य च ॥
शुद्धिः संक्षेपणाज्ज्ञेया पलालेन्धनयोस्तथा ॥ 7 ॥
मार्जनाद्वेश्मनां शुद्धिः क्षितौ शोधनतः क्षणात् ॥
संमार्जितेन तोयेन वाससां शुद्धिरिष्यते ॥ ॥ 8 ॥
बहूनां प्रोक्षणाच्छुद्धिः धान्यानां च विनिर्दिशेत् ॥
शुद्धिर्द्रुमाणा विज्ञेया नित्यसत्पवनेन तु ॥ 9 ॥
प्रोक्षणात्संहतानां तु दारवाणां च तक्षणात् ॥
सिद्धार्थकाणां कल्केन शृङ्गदन्तमयस्य च ॥ 2.79.10 ॥
गोवालैः फलपत्राणामस्थ्नां स्याच्छृङ्गवस्तथा ॥
निर्यासानां गुडानां च लवणानां तथैव च ॥ 11 ॥
कुसुम्भकुंकुमानां च ऊर्णाकार्पासयोस्तथा ॥
प्रोक्षणात्कथिता शुद्धिरित्याह भगवान् हि सः ॥ 12 ॥
भूमिष्ठमुदकं शुद्धं तथैव च शिलागतम् ॥
वर्णगन्धरसैर्दुष्टैर्वर्जितं यदि तद्भवेत् ॥ 13 ॥
2.16.m:
The purification of beds, seats, vehicles, / sacrificial wooden swords, winnowing baskets, and carts, / as well as of straw and firewood, is known to be by sprinkling.
The purification of houses is by sweeping, and immediately on the ground by cleansing; / the purification of clothes is held to be with swept-clean water.
One should prescribe the purification of a large quantity of grains by sprinkling; / the purification of trees is known to be by the constant good breeze.
Of stacked things, [purification is] by sprinkling; of wooden objects, by planing; / and of objects made of horn or ivory, with a paste of white mustard.
The purification of fruits and leaves is by cow-hair, and of bones it is like that of horn; / and likewise of resins, jaggery, and salt,
and of safflower and saffron, as well as of wool and cotton, / purification is declared to be by sprinkling; so indeed said the Blessed Lord.
Water on the ground is pure, and likewise water lying upon stone, / provided that it is free from corrupt color, smell, and taste.

2.16.s:
śuddhaṃ nadīgataṃ toyaṃ sarva eva tathākarāḥ ..
śuddhaṃ prasāritaṃ paṇyaṃ śuddhe cāśvājayormukhe .. 14 ..
mukhavarjaṃ ca gauḥ śuddhā mārjāraḥ śvā ca no śuciḥ ..
śayyā bhāryā śiśurvastramupavītaṃ kamaṇḍaluḥ .. .. 15 ..
ātmanaḥ kathitaṃ śuddhaṃ na parasya kathañcana ..
nārīṇāṃ caiva vatsānāṃ śakunīnāṃ śunāṃ mukham .. 16 ..
ratau prasravaṇe vṛkṣe mṛgayāyāṃ sadā śuciḥ ..
śuddhā bhartuścaturthe'hni snātā nārī rajasvalā .. 17 ..
daivakarmaṇi pitrye ca pañcame'hani śudhyati ..
kṛtvā mūtrapurīṣaṃ vā snātvā bhoktumanāstathā .. 18 .!
bhuktvā kṣuttvā tathā suptvā pītvā cāmbho'vagāhya ca ..
rathyāmākramya vācāmedvāso viparidhāya ca .. 19 ..
kṛtvā mūtrapurīṣaṃ ca lepagandhāpahaṃ budhaḥ ..
uddhṛtenāmbhasā śaucaṃ mṛdā śaucaṃ samācaret .. 2.79.20 ..
2.16.d:
शुद्धं नदीगतं तोयं सर्व एव तथाकराः ॥
शुद्धं प्रसारितं पण्यं शुद्धे चाश्वाजयोर्मुखे ॥ 14 ॥
मुखवर्जं च गौः शुद्धा मार्जारः श्वा च नो शुचिः ॥
शय्या भार्या शिशुर्वस्त्रमुपवीतं कमण्डलुः ॥ ॥ 15 ॥
आत्मनः कथितं शुद्धं न परस्य कथञ्चन ॥
नारीणां चैव वत्सानां शकुनीनां शुनां मुखम् ॥ 16 ॥
रतौ प्रस्रवणे वृक्षे मृगयायां सदा शुचिः ॥
शुद्धा भर्तुश्चतुर्थेऽह्नि स्नाता नारी रजस्वला ॥ 17 ॥
दैवकर्मणि पित्र्ये च पञ्चमेऽहनि शुध्यति ॥
कृत्वा मूत्रपुरीषं वा स्नात्वा भोक्तुमनास्तथा ॥ 18 ।!
भुक्त्वा क्षुत्त्वा तथा सुप्त्वा पीत्वा चाम्भोऽवगाह्य च ॥
रथ्यामाक्रम्य वाचामेद्वासो विपरिधाय च ॥ 19 ॥
कृत्वा मूत्रपुरीषं च लेपगन्धापहं बुधः ॥
उद्धृतेनाम्भसा शौचं मृदा शौचं समाचरेत् ॥ 2.79.20 ॥
2.16.m:
Water in a river is pure, and so are all mines. / Merchandise displayed [for sale] is pure, and pure are the mouths of a horse and a goat.
A cow is pure except for its mouth; a cat and a dog are not pure. / One's own bed, wife, child, garment, sacred thread, and water-pot
are declared pure for oneself, never for another. / The mouth of women, of calves, of birds, and of dogs
is always pure in lovemaking, in nursing, in [picking fruit from] a tree, and in hunting. / A menstruating woman is pure for her husband on the fourth day after bathing;
she becomes pure for rites to gods and ancestors on the fifth day. / Having discharged urine or feces, or having bathed, or wishing to eat, / having eaten, sneezed, slept, drunk water, bathed [in a river], / walked on a public street, or changed clothes, one should sip water [for purification].
Having discharged urine or feces, the wise man should perform purification / that removes smears and odor, with water drawn up and with earth.

2.16.s:
mehane mṛttikāḥ pañca liṅge dve parikīrtite ..
ekasminviṃśatirhaste dvayo jñeyāścaturdaśa .. 21 ..
tisrastu mṛttikā jñeyāḥ kṛtvā tu nakhaśodhanam ..
tisrastisraḥ pādayośca śaucakāmaistu nityadā .. 22 ..
śaucametadgṛhasthānāṃ dviguṇaṃ brahmacāriṇām ..
triguṇaṃ tu vanasthānāṃ yatīnāṃ ca caturguṇam .. 23 ..
mṛttikā ca vinirdiṣṭā tripūrvaṃ pūryate yayā ..
śuddhiśca kācabhāṇḍānāṃ kevalena tathāmbhasā .. 24 ..
śrīphalairaṃśupaṭṭānāṃ kṣaumāṇāṃ gaurasarṣapaiḥ ..
śuddhiḥ padmākṣatoyena mṛgalomnāṃ prakīrtitā ..
puṣpāṇāṃ candanānāṃ ca prokṣaṇācchuddhiriṣyate .. 25 ..
siddhārthakaiḥ śuddhimudāharanti lomnāṃ tathā bhārgavavaṃśamukhya ..
sarvasya jīvasya viśuddhiruktā mṛdā ca toyena vigandhalepāt ..26..
2.16.d:
मेहने मृत्तिकाः पञ्च लिङ्गे द्वे परिकीर्तिते ॥
एकस्मिन्विंशतिर्हस्ते द्वयो ज्ञेयाश्चतुर्दश ॥ 21 ॥
तिस्रस्तु मृत्तिका ज्ञेयाः कृत्वा तु नखशोधनम् ॥
तिस्रस्तिस्रः पादयोश्च शौचकामैस्तु नित्यदा ॥ 22 ॥
शौचमेतद्गृहस्थानां द्विगुणं ब्रह्मचारिणाम् ॥
त्रिगुणं तु वनस्थानां यतीनां च चतुर्गुणम् ॥ 23 ॥
मृत्तिका च विनिर्दिष्टा त्रिपूर्वं पूर्यते यया ॥
शुद्धिश्च काचभाण्डानां केवलेन तथाम्भसा ॥ 24 ॥
श्रीफलैरंशुपट्टानां क्षौमाणां गौरसर्षपैः ॥
शुद्धिः पद्माक्षतोयेन मृगलोम्नां प्रकीर्तिता ॥
पुष्पाणां चन्दनानां च प्रोक्षणाच्छुद्धिरिष्यते ॥ 25 ॥
सिद्धार्थकैः शुद्धिमुदाहरन्ति लोम्नां तथा भार्गववंशमुख्य ॥
सर्वस्य जीवस्य विशुद्धिरुक्ता मृदा च तोयेन विगन्धलेपात् ॥26॥
2.16.m:
Five lumps of earth are prescribed for urination, two for the penis. / On one hand twenty [are prescribed], and on both hands fourteen should be known.
Three lumps of earth should be known after cleaning the nails, / and three for each foot by those who always desire purity.
This is the purification for householders; it is double for celibate students, / threefold for forest-dwellers, and fourfold for ascetics.
The earth is prescribed as that by which the first three [fingers] are filled. / And the purification of glass vessels is with water alone.
The purification of silk cloths is with bilva fruits; of linen, with white mustard; / of deer-hair [fabrics], it is declared to be with water containing lotus seeds. / Purification of flowers and sandalwoods is considered to be by sprinkling.
They declare the purification of wool with white mustard seeds, O head of the Bhṛgu lineage; / purification of all living beings is stated to be with earth and water through removal of odor and smear.

2.80 / Rāma said: / You know all this concerning the classes and stages of life. / Puṣkara said: / Non-violence, truthfulness in speech, compassion toward living beings,
visiting pilgrimage sites, charity, celibacy, absence of malice, / service to gods and twice-born, and to teachers, O foremost of the Bhṛgus,
hearing all dharmas, worship of the ancestors, / constant devotion to the king, and using good scriptures as one's eyes,
gentleness, forbearance, and piety— / this common dharma has been declared to you, O best of the Bhṛgus.
Sacrificing, officiating at sacrifices, giving gifts, teaching, / acceptance of gifts, and studying: these are designated as the duties of a brahmin.
Giving gifts, studying, and sacrificing according to rule: / this duty is proclaimed for a kṣatriya and a vaiśya.
The special duty of a kṣatriya is the protection of subjects. / Agriculture, cattle-rearing, and trade are proclaimed for a vaiśya.

2.16.m:
Service to the twice-born and all crafts are for a śūdra. / The brahmin, kṣatriya, and vaiśya—these three classes are the twice-born.
Their second birth should be known as the binding of the muñjā girdle. / There, the teacher is the father and the Sāvitrī is the mother / in the birth through the binding of the muñjā girdle for brahmins, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas.
By conduct, twice-born men are equal to śūdras as long as they are not proficient in the Veda, O Rāma; / after that, they obtain the status of the twice-born and preside as deities over all duties.

जीवेत्क्षत्रियधर्मेण सा ह्यस्य वृत्त्यनन्तरा ॥ 1 ॥
उभाभ्यामप्यजीवन्वै वैश्यवृत्तिं समाचरेत् ॥
ब्राह्मणः क्षत्त्रियो वैश्यः शूद्रवृत्तिं विवर्जयेत् ॥ ॥ 2 ॥
शूद्रो ब्राह्मणवृत्तिं च विशेषेण विवर्जयेत् ॥
आजीवत्सु स वृत्या च मध्यवृत्तिं समाचरेत् ॥ 3 ॥
ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियो वापि वैश्यवृत्त्या तु वर्तयन् ॥
अयः शस्त्रं विषं मांसं सोमं गन्धांश्च सर्वशः ॥ 4 ॥
क्षीरं क्षौद्रं दधि घृतं तैलं मज्जां गुडं कुशम् ॥

रसा रसैर्निहन्तव्या गन्धेन लवणं रसैः ॥ 6 ॥
2.17.m:
The king must guard at his own proper time against this terrible intermixture of men; / for kingdoms together with their kings perish on incurring terrible intermixtures.
2.82 / Puṣkara said: / Unable to make a living by his own prescribed work, a brahmin / may live by the dharma of a kṣatriya, for that is the occupation immediately next to his.
Unable to live even by both, he may certainly adopt the occupation of a vaiśya. / A brahmin, a kṣatriya, or a vaiśya should avoid the occupation of a śūdra.
And a śūdra should especially avoid the occupation of a brahmin. / When [others] are unable to maintain their livelihoods, he may adopt an intermediate occupation.
A brahmin or a kṣatriya who makes his living by the occupation of a vaiśya / [should not sell] iron, weapons, poison, meat, soma, and perfumes of all kinds,
milk, honey, curds, ghee, oil, bone marrow, molasses, kuśa grass, / liquor, indigo, lac, salt, and living beings.
He should never sell sesame seeds, cooked food, or dairy products. / Flavours may be exchanged for flavours, perfumes for salt, [and salt] for flavours;

वैश्यो वा क्षत्त्रियो वापि वर्जयेद्द्विजजीविकाम् ॥7 ॥

इतरेषां हि पण्यानां विक्रयां मनुजोत्तम ॥
ब्राह्मणः सप्तरात्रेण वैश्यभावं हि गच्छति ॥9॥
क्षिप्राणि यानि रूक्षाणि चराणि च मृदूनि च ॥
वाणिज्ये तानि शस्यन्ते तिथिं रिक्तां विवर्जयेत् ॥2.82.1 0 ॥ ॥
द्विकं शतं तु गृह्णीयात्कुसीदेनापि वर्धयन् ॥
ततोऽधिकं तु गृह्णानश्चौरस्याप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥ 11 ॥
प्रतिपद्द्वादशी षष्ठी नक्षत्राणि ध्रुवाणि च ॥
कुसीदे वर्जनीयानि नित्यं सूर्यसुतस्य च॥12॥
कृषिभूमिपतेर्भागं दत्त्वा कुर्याद्यथोदितम् ॥
ध्रुवाणि सौम्यं मैत्रं च वायव्यं पौष्ण्माश्विनम्॥ ॥.13॥
2.17.m:
and cooked food for cooked food, and sesame for an equal quantity of grain. / A vaiśya or a kṣatriya should also avoid the livelihood of a twice-born [brahmin].
A brahmin falls immediately by [selling] meat, lac, and salt; / and after three days he becomes a śūdra by selling milk.
Indeed, by selling other commodities, O best of men, / a brahmin attains the condition of a vaiśya within seven nights.
Those [lunar mansions] that are swift, harsh, movable, and gentle / are praised in trade; one should avoid an empty lunar day.
Increasing [wealth] even through usury, he may take two percent [a month]; / but taking more than that, he incurs the guilt of a thief.
The first, twelfth, and sixth lunar days, fixed asterisms, / and [the day] of the son of the Sun should always be avoided in usury.
Having given the share of the lord of the earth, he should practice agriculture as prescribed. / The fixed [asterisms], the Saumya, Maitra, Vāyavya, Pauṣṇa, Āśvina,

vāsavaṃ śravaṇaṃ citrā viśākhā mūlameva ca ..

kṛṣyārambhe prayatnena tithiṃ riktāṃ vivarjayeta..
aṅgārakadinaṃ varjyaṃ divasaṃ sūryajasya ca .. 15 ..

अङ्गारकदिनं वर्ज्यं दिवसं सूर्यजस्य च ॥ 15 ॥
2.17.m: At the beginning of farming, one should diligently avoid an empty lunar day. / Tuesday is to be avoided, as is the day of the son of the Sun.

nakṣatrāṇāṃ yathoktānāṃ muhūrteṣu ca kārayet ..
muhurte yadi vā brāhme sarvakarmasu pūjite..16..

2.17.m: One should carry it out during the muhūrtas of the aforesaid asterisms, / or during the brāhma-muhūrta, which is praised in all rites.

varāhaṃ pūjeyaddevaṃ śeṣaṃ pṛthvīṃ tathaiva ca ..
parjanyaṃ bhāskaraṃ vāyuṃ deveśaṃ śaśinaṃ tathā .. 17 ..

2.17.m: One should worship the divine Boar, Śeṣa, and likewise the Earth, / Parjanya, the Sun, the Wind, the Lord of the Gods, and the Moon,

2.17.m: and the ploughshare and the pair of oxen, with an abundance of perfume, garlands, and food. / Then one should make an offering in a well-kindled fire,

devatānāṃ yathoktānāṃ juhuyācca ghṛtāhutīḥ ..
gāvo bhaga iti dvābhyāṃ sīrāṃ yuñjantyatastribhiḥ .. 19 ..

गावो भग इति द्वाभ्यां सीरां युञ्जन्त्यतस्त्रिभिः ॥ 19 ॥
2.17.m: and offer oblations of ghee to the aforesaid deities, / with the two [verses beginning] 'The cows are fortune', and then yoke the plough with the three [beginning] 'They yoke the ploughs'.

2.17.s:
phālaṃ śunāṃ suphāleti lāṅgalaṃ ca tatheti vai ..
hutvā viprānsamabhyarcya dakṣiṇābhiryathāvidhi .. 2.82.20 ..

2.17.m: Having offered to the ploughshare with '[May] the ploughshares [plough] happily' and likewise to the plough, / and having honoured the brahmins with sacrificial fees according to rule,

pūrvodakpravaṇāṃ bhūmiṃ vāhayetprāgghalena tu ..

2.17.m: Better is one's own dharma, though deficient, than the dharma of another well-performed. / Death in one's own dharma is better; the dharma of another is fraught with fear.

2.17.m:
Thus ends the eighty-second chapter, named 'Rules for Times of Adversity', in the second book of the illustrious Viṣṇudharmottara, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the narrative of Puṣkara to Rāma.
2.83 / Rāma said: / Tell me the optional rite by which trade is purified, / and by what rite one obtains an abundant harvest.
Puṣkara said: / Fasting under the asterism Mūla, the domestic priest should perform this rite / for him who has fasted and is ever striving for victory, O knower of dharma.
When the moon reaches Uttarāṣāḍhā, he should bathe the man facing east / with four water-jars containing the root of the vetasa cane, conches, pearls,
and jewels according to availability, and likewise gold, / without cutting the roots, O delight of the Bhṛgus.
With new [offerings] he should worship the god who bears the conch, discus, and mace, / and likewise Pūrvāṣāḍhā, the Waters, Varuṇa, and the Moon,
with an abundance of perfumes, garlands, salutations, incense, lamps, and food. / In their names he should offer ghee, O twice-born.

2.17.d:
नीलवासावृतो भूत्वा क्षिपेदप्सु समाहितः॥
नीलानि राम वासांसि पयांसि विविधानि च॥7॥
तदा मंथं सुरां चैव मैरेयं विविधं तथा॥
शुक्लानि चैव माल्यानि धूपं दद्यात्तु कम्बुना॥8॥
तिम्यस्थि मकरादस्थि शङ्खमुक्ताफले तथा॥
सुवर्णान्तरितं कृत्वा धारयेच्च तथा मणिम्॥9॥
कृत्वैतत्सिद्धिमाप्नोति वाणिज्ये नात्र संशयः॥
समुद्रयाने च तथा कान्तारे न विषीदति॥2.83.10॥
नीलानि राम वासांसि दक्षिणा चात्र शस्यते॥
शङ्खं सुवर्णं रूप्यं च तथा मुक्ताफलानि च॥11॥
होत्रे कर्त्रे द्विजेभ्यश्च सर्वमेतद्विधीयते॥
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेच्चात्र परमान्नं तु संस्कृतम्॥12॥
अलंघयन्नित्यमथाप्यमृक्षं करोति कर्मैतदतन्द्रितात्मा॥
न जातु लाभाद्विनिवर्ततेऽसौ समुद्रमार्गादिव निम्नगा वै॥ 13॥
2.17.m:
Clothed in blue garments and composed in mind, he should cast into the waters,
O Rāma, blue clothes and various kinds of milk,
then groats, liquor, and various kinds of intoxicating drink,
as well as white garlands, and he should offer incense from a conch.
The bone of a timi-fish, the bone of a makara, a conch, and pearls,
enclosed in gold, and a jewel likewise, he should wear.
Having done this, he attains success in commerce—there is no doubt of this;
likewise, when travelling by sea and in the wilderness, he does not despair.
Blue clothes, O Rāma, are recommended here as the sacrificial fee,
as well as a conch, gold, silver, and pearls.
All this is prescribed for the Hotṛ priest, the officiant, and the twice-born;
and here he should feed brahmins with prepared rice-milk.
Not neglecting this constellation, the unwearied man who always performs this rite
never turns away from gain, just as a river [never turns back] from its course to the ocean.

2.17.m:
Thus ends the eighty-third chapter, entitled 'Description of the Bath on Pūrvāṣāḍhā', in the dialogue between Puṣkara and Rāma, in the compilation of Mārkaṇḍeya, in the second book of the illustrious Viṣṇudharmottara.
Puṣkara said:
Having fasted well himself, the learned man should always cause the sacrificer, who has fasted,
to bathe under Mūla, while he stands facing the proper direction.
Bathed with two sturdy jars filled with dūrvā-grass, kuśa-grass, and śamī-leaves,
he should then worship the Slayer of Madhu,
Virūpākṣa together with Varuṇa, the Moon, and Mūla as well,
with an abundance of perfumes, garlands, salutations, incenses, lamps, and food.
O twice-born, he should offer clarified butter in their names alone;
then, dressed in yellow clothes, with fish, mash, and pork,
combined with liquor and spiced rice-porridge, standing facing the direction prescribed for bathing,
he should place his knee on the ground and offer an oblation to Nirṛti.
Then with eighteen flowers and five roots,
the wise man should wear on his head a jewel containing gold inside.

राम उवाच ॥

त्वं हि वेत्थ महाभाग सर्वधर्मान्यथाविधि ॥ 1 ॥

षोडशर्तु निशाः स्त्रीणामाद्यास्तिस्रस्तु गर्हिताः ॥
व्रजेद्युग्मासु पुत्रार्थी ततः परमिति श्रुतिः ॥ 2 ॥

दीर्घायुषो धर्मपरा भवन्तीह धनान्विताः ॥

2.17.m:
Having performed this entire rite, he obtains agriculture yielding abundant fruit;
and here roots and fruits should be given as the sacrificial fee,
as well as yellow garments, gold, and silver;
and food desired by the brahmins should be given here.
Not neglecting Mūla, O foremost of the lineage of Bhṛgu, performing this bath always,
the wise man invariably attains the agriculture he desires; there is no question about this.
Rāma said:
I wish to hear from you the path of dharma; speak to me.
For you, O noble one, know all the dharmas according to rule.
Puṣkara said:
The nights of the fertile season of women are sixteen; the first three are condemned.
One desiring a son should approach [his wife] on the even [nights] thereafter—such is the sacred tradition.
Likewise, O Rāma, one desiring a daughter should approach the woman on the odd [nights].
Those [begotten] on the distant even nights are praised: they are pleasant to behold,
long-lived, devoted to dharma, and endowed with wealth in this world.
In the establishment of the conception of the embryo, the rite of impregnation is prescribed.

षष्ठेऽष्टमे वा सीमन्तकर्मस्वेतेषु च त्रिषु ॥ 5 ॥
पुन्नामधेयं नक्षत्रं पुत्रकामस्य शस्यते ॥
